title: Published multi-targeted .NET class library (NuGet)

versions.latest: .NET 10 (LTS, active); .NET 8 and 9 reach end of support 2026-11-10
built into the .NET 8+ SDK (CI builds with SDK 10.0.x)

rules.rule: Never add a parameter to an existing public method, not even an optional one (including `CancellationToken cancellationToken = default`). Add a new overload and have the old one call it.
rules.why: Optional parameters are compiled into the caller. A consumer built against the old signature throws MissingMethodException at runtime once it gets the new package, for example through a transitive upgrade. Package validation reports this as CP0002.

rules.rule: Minimise breaking changes even in 0.x, because this is a low/middle-level client library. Do not rename or remove public types, members or parameters (a change in parameter case counts). Do not change a member's type, seal a public class, make a member static or non-static, or add members to ITransloaditSerializer. To retire an API, first put [Obsolete("<what to use instead>")] on it and ship at least one release with both the old and new API. Remove it only in a release that is declared breaking, with a reviewed CompatibilitySuppressions.xml entry and a release note. Leave new behaviour that affects existing users off by default, behind an option.
rules.why: Each of these is a binary or source break for consumers compiled against the previous package, including libraries that depend on this one and that the end user cannot fix. ITransloaditSerializer is an extension point (TransloaditClientOptions.Serializer), so a new member breaks every custom implementation.
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: the repo ships breaking changes in 0.x minor bumps with no [Obsolete] step (e.g. commit e28fe29 / #29 removed the snake_case naming convention from both serializers outright), and no [Obsolete] attribute exists anywhere in src/Transloadit. SemVer item 4 permits this in 0.y.z, but it is weaker than the library guidance. Fix: obsolete-then-remove for every public API change, gated by package validation (rule 4), with each accepted break listed in CompatibilitySuppressions.xml and the release notes.

rules.rule: Give every TFM the same public API. Keep `#if TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT` / `#if NET452` around implementation code and internal types only. Never wrap a public type or member in them.
rules.why: netstandard2.0 is compatible with net461, and net461 is one of the shipped assets. Say a consumer's netstandard2.0 library calls SystemTextJsonSerializer and runs inside a net461 app. NuGet picks the net461 asset, which has no such type, and the call fails at runtime with TypeLoadException/MissingMethodException. The compatible-framework validator reports this as CP0001/CP0002 at pack time.
where: src/Transloadit/Serialization/NewtonsoftJsonSerializer.cs NewtonsoftJsonSerializer, TransloaditSerializerSettings.cs, AnyOfConverter.cs, BooleanToIntConverter.cs, DateTimeConverters.cs (public, only under TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT)

rules.rule: Turn on package validation in the library project: EnablePackageValidation=true, plus PackageValidationBaselineVersion set to the last version published to nuget.org. Commit a reviewed CompatibilitySuppressions.xml for every break you accept on purpose (generate it with ApiCompatGenerateSuppressionFile=true). After each release, move the baseline to that release.
rules.why: Nothing in the build or CI currently compares the API against the previous release or across TFMs. A binary break or a dropped TFM ships silently. Validation runs on `dotnet pack`, which deploy.yml already runs.
where: not used here yet: src/Transloadit/Transloadit.csproj has no EnablePackageValidation

rules.rule: Remember that every conditional PackageReference in the library (including those in Directory.Build.props) becomes a dependency group that consumers of that TFM inherit. Give each one a minimum version only (no exact pin, no upper bound). Mark build-only packages PrivateAssets="All". Remove references the code does not use.
rules.why: Consumers on net452/net461 get System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation 4.3.0 as a transitive dependency, but no code in src/ uses RuntimeInformation. That adds a diamond-dependency and binding-redirect risk for nothing. Raising the System.Text.Json floor raises it for every netstandard2.0/net462-net7.0 consumer.
rules.repoConvention: Sound: Microsoft.SourceLink.GitHub and Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies are marked PrivateAssets="All", so they never become consumer dependencies, which matches the guidance. Keep it.

rules.rule: Publish symbols as a .snupkg to nuget.org (IncludeSymbols=true, SymbolPackageFormat=snupkg, DebugType=portable) instead of embedding them. Rely on the SDK's built-in Source Link (the .NET 8+ SDK covers GitHub) instead of pinning Microsoft.SourceLink.GitHub. Pack only from Release, where ContinuousIntegrationBuild and Deterministic are set.
rules.why: Embedded PDBs make the assembly larger for every consumer and slow restore and load, whether anyone debugs or not. A .snupkg serves symbols on demand from the nuget.org symbol server. Referencing any Source Link package in an SDK 8+ project overrides the SDK's bundled version, so the 8.0.0 pin freezes Source Link while CI builds with SDK 10.0.x. A Debug pack is non-deterministic (Deterministic=false), so the published binary cannot be matched to its commit.
where: .github/workflows/deploy.yml (dotnet build/pack -c Release, dotnet nuget push nuget/*.nupkg)
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: the repo embeds portable PDBs in the DLL (DebugType=embedded, IncludeSymbols=false in src/Transloadit/Transloadit.csproj) and pins Microsoft.SourceLink.GitHub 8.0.0. Fix: set DebugType=portable, IncludeSymbols=true and SymbolPackageFormat=snupkg. Check that deploy.yml pushes the .snupkg next to the .nupkg (dotnet nuget push picks up the matching .snupkg automatically). Drop the Microsoft.SourceLink.GitHub reference, or keep it current on purpose.

rules.rule: Strong-name the assembly on every TFM, because the targets include .NET Framework and netstandard2.0. Check the key pair (public + private) into source control, or check in the public key and use PublicSign, and set AssemblyOriginatorKeyFile. Give InternalsVisibleTo the test assembly name plus its public key, and sign the test assembly too. Choose the key once and never add, remove or change it afterwards.
rules.why: An unsigned assembly cannot be referenced by strong-named .NET Framework apps and libraries. Adding, removing or changing the key changes assembly identity and breaks all compiled consumers, so the cheapest moment to adopt it is before 1.0. Shipping both a signed and an unsigned package forks the ecosystem.
where: src/Transloadit/Transloadit.csproj SignAssembly=True (no AssemblyOriginatorKeyFile, no .snk in repo)
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: the strong-naming state is inconsistent. The csproj sets SignAssembly=True with no AssemblyOriginatorKeyFile and no .snk in the repo. InternalsVisibleTo("Transloadit.Tests") names an unsigned friend without a public key, which the compiler rejects for a strong-named assembly. CLAUDE.md claims the assembly is signed. Most likely the shipped DLL is not strong-named (inference, not checked against a built DLL). Fix: add a key (committed .snk or public key + PublicSign), set AssemblyOriginatorKeyFile, sign the test project and give InternalsVisibleTo its public key, and announce the identity change in a release declared breaking. Do it before 1.0 if possible.

rules.rule: Version the package with SemVer 2.0.0. Set AssemblyVersion to the major version only (Major.0.0.0), keeping its major in sync with the package major, and never leave it fixed across majors. Put the CI build number in FileVersion (Major.Minor.Build.Revision). Let Source Link generate InformationalVersion. Bump <Version> and ClientVersion.Current together.
rules.why: On .NET Framework a strong-named reference must match AssemblyVersion exactly. Changing it on every minor or patch forces binding redirects on consumers and on libraries that depend on this one. ProjectTests fails when Version and ClientVersion.Current differ. deploy.yml tags v<Version> and pushes with --skip-duplicate, so redeploying without a bump publishes nothing and gives no error.
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: AssemblyVersion defaults to the full package version (0.11.0.0), and ProjectTests.TestAssemblyVersion_ShouldMatch_ClientVersionCurrent asserts that its first 3 parts equal ClientVersion.Current, so it changes on every release. Fix: set AssemblyVersion=$(Major).0.0.0 and FileVersion with a CI revision. Change ProjectTests to compare ClientVersion.Current with the package version, i.e. AssemblyInformationalVersion before the '+' commit suffix. This matters together with adopting strong naming (rule 7). How to handle major 0 is an open question.

rules.rule: Make HttpClient ownership explicit and long-lived. TransloaditClient builds `new HttpClient()` when TransloaditClientOptions.HttpClient is null and never disposes it, so every documented example must create TransloaditClient once and reuse it, or pass in a shared HttpClient. On net5+ that is a SocketsHttpHandler with PooledConnectionLifetime; on .NET Framework, IHttpClientFactory. Never dispose a caller-supplied HttpClient.
rules.why: Creating a client per request gives each request its own connection pool. Under load the OS runs out of ports (SocketException). A long-lived client with no PooledConnectionLifetime never notices DNS changes. Disposing a client the caller owns breaks the caller's other requests.
where: readme.md NotificationsController sample (builds a new TransloaditClient in a field initializer, i.e. once per controller instance)
tests/Transloadit.Tests/Tests/TestBase.cs TestBase (two clients per test instance)

rules.rule: Do not mutate objects the caller owns. Set the Transloadit-Client header on each HttpRequestMessage, not on the caller's HttpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders. Copy dictionaries such as the parameters passed to GetSignedSmartCdnUrl before adding auth_key/exp. Keep BuildRequest's approach of building a fresh AuthParams and restoring the caller's object.
rules.why: DefaultRequestHeaders is not on HttpClient's thread-safe list. Mutating it on a shared or factory client races with in-flight requests and adds the header to every other host that client calls. Writing into the caller's dictionary leaks auth_key and a stale exp into their next call.

rules.rule: Put .ConfigureAwait(false) on every await in src/Transloadit, and never block on a task (.Result, .Wait(), GetAwaiter().GetResult()) inside the library.
rules.why: Library code runs under whatever SynchronizationContext the caller has (WinForms/WPF, classic ASP.NET on net4x). Capturing it costs performance, and if the caller blocks on the task it deadlocks.
rules.repoConvention: Sound: .editorconfig sets CA2007 to error, so a missing ConfigureAwait fails the build in the net5+ inner builds, where .NET analyzers run by default. The CA2007 docs describe exactly this rule for app-independent libraries. Keep it.

rules.rule: Add cancellation as new overloads that take `CancellationToken cancellationToken` as the last parameter. Forward the token to HttpClient.SendAsync and Task.Delay. Have the old overloads pass CancellationToken.None. When cancellation ends the work, let OperationCanceledException propagate so the task ends Canceled; do not wrap it or return a result.
rules.why: No public async method accepts a token today. Callers cannot abort an upload or a polling loop, so their shutdown and request-abort paths hang until HttpClient.Timeout or WaitCompletionTimeout. Adding the token as an optional parameter instead would be a binary break (rule 1).
where: src/Transloadit/Utilities/AssemblyTracker.cs WaitCompletionAsync (Task.Delay uses only the internal timeout token)

rules.rule: When a TFM is missing an API, bridge the gap in src/Transloadit/Polyfills (internal, guarded by the narrowest #if) or pick an API that exists on every shipped TFM. Check the API's 'Applies to' list before using it.
rules.why: Code that compiles for net10.0 can fail to compile for net452/netstandard2.0 inner builds (TreatWarningsAsErrors), or quietly behave differently. For example, CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals exists only from netcoreapp2.1/netstandard2.1.

rules.rule: Target only supported platforms. Use netstandard2.0 for broad compatibility, net462 for .NET Framework 4.6.2-4.7.1 users, and the in-support modern .NET versions (net8.0 and later; net10.0 once net8.0/net9.0 end support on 2026-11-10). Leave CheckEolTargetFramework at its default so an EOL target warns. Dropping a TFM is still a breaking change: do it explicitly, in a release declared breaking, with the baseline validator's report suppressed and documented.
rules.why: Out-of-support targets have no security servicing, and they cost polyfills, a second serializer code path, and assets no test runs. If a TFM is removed silently, consumers pinned to it fail restore or fall back to the netstandard2.0 asset, which has different dependencies.
rules.repoConvention: Known deviation: the repo targets net452 and net461 (retired 2022-04-26) and net5.0, net6.0 and net7.0 (out of support), and silences the SDK warning with CheckEolTargetFramework=false in src/Transloadit/Transloadit.csproj. net8.0 and net9.0 leave support 2026-11-10, and net462 on 2027-01-12. Fix: plan a release declared breaking that removes the out-of-support TFMs (keeping netstandard2.0 + net462 for .NET Framework reach) and removes CheckEolTargetFramework=false. Accept the baseline validator's dropped-TFM report in CompatibilitySuppressions.xml and the release notes. Until then, do not add new EOL targets.

rules.rule: Keep the nuget.org Trusted Publishing policy and the workflow in lock-step: same workflow file name (deploy.yml), same environment (Release), and `id-token: write` granted only to the publish job. Request the temporary key immediately before the push.
rules.why: Renaming the workflow file or the environment makes the OIDC token stop matching the policy, and publishing fails at release time. The temporary key is single-use and valid for 1 hour. A broader id-token grant lets other jobs mint publish credentials.
where: .github/workflows/deploy.yml job publish (NuGet/login@v1, permissions id-token: write, environment: Release)

bugCategories.name: binary-break-in-public-api
bugCategories.lookFor: Diffs to public signatures: an added optional parameter, a renamed or re-cased parameter, a changed return/property type, a removed or renamed public type or member without a prior [Obsolete] release, a new interface member, a newly sealed class, a changed public const/enum value.
bugCategories.failure: Consumers compiled against the previous package throw MissingMethodException/TypeLoadException at runtime after a transitive upgrade, or fail to compile.

bugCategories.name: tfm-api-divergence
bugCategories.lookFor: Public types or members inside #if TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT, #if NET452 or other TFM symbols; a conditional PackageReference whose condition list misses a TFM.
bugCategories.failure: Code built against the netstandard2.0 asset fails at runtime on the net461 asset (missing type), or one TFM ships without a dependency it needs.

bugCategories.name: httpclient-per-call
bugCategories.lookFor: `new TransloaditClient(...)` or `new HttpClient()` per request, per controller instance or per test; library code that disposes options.HttpClient.
bugCategories.failure: Socket/port exhaustion (SocketException) under load, or the caller's shared HttpClient disposed under them.

bugCategories.name: caller-object-mutation
bugCategories.lookFor: Writes to caller-supplied objects: HttpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders, dictionaries passed in (SmartCdnService parameters), request param objects not restored in a finally.
bugCategories.failure: Races with in-flight requests on a shared client, a header leaked to other hosts, a stale exp/auth_key reused on the caller's next call.

bugCategories.name: context-capture-or-sync-over-async
bugCategories.lookFor: An await without .ConfigureAwait(false) (CA2007 suppressed), .Result/.Wait()/GetAwaiter().GetResult() inside src/Transloadit.
bugCategories.failure: Deadlock when a WinForms/WPF or classic ASP.NET caller blocks on a library task; extra context switches otherwise.

bugCategories.name: cancellation-not-honoured
bugCategories.lookFor: Async paths that cannot be cancelled, or a token accepted but not forwarded (CA2016). Timeouts built from an options value that can be 0: AssemblyTracker.MergeOptions uses `options?.WaitCompletionTimeout ?? 30000`, which yields 0 when an options object is passed without a timeout, so CancellationTokenSource(0) cancels immediately.
bugCategories.failure: Calls that cannot be aborted, or a WaitCompletionAsync that throws OperationCanceledException on its first poll whenever AssemblyTrackerOptions is supplied without WaitCompletionTimeout.

bugCategories.name: non-constant-time-signature-compare
bugCategories.lookFor: Signature or HMAC comparison with == / string.Equals, or an early-exit loop, in code that verifies untrusted input (webhook notifications).
bugCategories.failure: A timing side channel that lets an attacker forge a valid signature byte by byte, so the receiving endpoint trusts forged Assembly notifications.

bugCategories.name: release-version-drift
bugCategories.lookFor: A Version bump without a ClientVersion.Current bump (or the reverse); a release PR with no Version bump; a minor/patch release that changes AssemblyVersion once strong naming is adopted; the Trusted Publishing workflow file or environment renamed.
bugCategories.failure: ProjectTests fails, the wrong Transloadit-Client header is sent, `--skip-duplicate` publishes nothing, .NET Framework consumers need new binding redirects, or the publish job is rejected by nuget.org.

testing.layers: Unit tests with FakeHttpMessageHandler/TestClientFactory prove the request pipeline (params, signature, header, empty-body handling) and cancellation/timeout behaviour offline. Live API tests (Tests/Api, need appsettings.Tests.json) prove wire compatibility. Package-level properties (identical API across TFMs, no break against the last release, dependency groups, readme/icon/license in the nupkg, the .snupkg) are proven only by `dotnet pack` with package validation enabled. No test does that today.
commands: dotnet pack src/Transloadit -c Release -p:EnablePackageValidation=true -p:PackageValidationBaselineVersion=<last published version>
traps: The test project targets net461;net462;net472;net48;net6.0-net10.0, so the net452, net5.0 and netstandard2.0 assets that ship are never executed by tests.

CI (tests.yml) runs only net8.0/net9.0/net10.0 and net462/net472/net48. net461, the only tested TFM on the Newtonsoft (TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT) path, never runs in CI. Run it locally for any serializer or pipeline change.
TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT is defined separately in the library csproj (net452, net461) and the test csproj (net461). Change both together.
AssemblyTrackerOfflineTests pins today's timeout behaviour (OperationCanceledException). Switching to TimeoutException is a behaviour break, not a refactor.
ProjectTests asserts AssemblyVersion == ClientVersion.Current. Moving AssemblyVersion to major-only (rule 8) requires changing that test to compare against the package/informational version.
Test parallelisation is disabled and API tests share account rate limits; do not add live tests where an offline FakeHttpMessageHandler test proves the same thing.

wiring.failure: ProjectTests fails; the client header reports the wrong version.

wiring.check: Every TFM in TargetFrameworks falls in exactly one serializer branch: TRANSLOADIT_NEWTONSOFT + Newtonsoft.Json (net452, net461), System.Text.Json 8.0.5 package (netstandard2.0, net462-net7.0), or in-box STJ (net8.0+).
wiring.failure: A new TFM compiles without a JSON dependency, or ships a duplicate one.

wiring.check: readme.md, LICENSE and icon.png are packed at the package root (None Pack=true PackagePath=/), matching PackageReadmeFile/PackageLicenseFile/PackageIcon.
wiring.failure: dotnet pack fails, or the package ships without license/readme.

wiring.check: The nuget.org Trusted Publishing policy names workflow file deploy.yml and environment Release, and the publish job has `id-token: write`.
wiring.failure: The publish step is rejected at release time.

wiring.check: SignAssembly comes with AssemblyOriginatorKeyFile pointing at a committed key (or PublicSign with the public key), and InternalsVisibleTo carries the signed test assembly's public key.
wiring.failure: The assembly ships unsigned despite SignAssembly=True (the current state), or tests lose access to internals once signing is real.

performance.note: One HttpClient per TransloaditClient: callers that keep a single TransloaditClient get connection reuse. On net5+, advise passing an HttpClient built on SocketsHttpHandler with PooledConnectionLifetime so DNS changes are picked up.

Embedded PDBs (the current DebugType=embedded, a known deviation; see rule 6) make the assembly larger for every consumer, affecting restore and load time whether or not anyone debugs. A .snupkg avoids that on nuget.org.
ConfigureAwait(false) avoids queueing every continuation back to the caller's context.

security.note: SignatureUtilities.ValidateSignature compares the computed and supplied HMAC with string ==, which leaks timing. It verifies untrusted webhook input (readme NotificationsController). Compare in constant time: CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals on netcoreapp2.1+/netstandard2.1, and an internal XOR-accumulate polyfill for net452-net48/netstandard2.0. Exposure is public and the stakes are auth, so treat a regression here as a blocker.

The System.Text.Json floor 8.0.5 is the patched version for CVE-2024-43485 (GHSA-8g4q-xg66-9fp4, JsonExtensionData DoS; 8.0.0-8.0.4 affected). Do not lower it. src/ does not use [JsonExtensionData] today. The advisory says .NET Framework apps need the package update, which this floor gives net462-net48 consumers.

Out-of-support target frameworks (net452, net461, net5.0-net7.0, soon net8.0/net9.0) receive no security servicing from Microsoft. Shipping assets for them invites consumers to stay on unpatched runtimes (see rule 13).
Publishing uses short-lived OIDC keys (Trusted Publishing) instead of a stored API key. Keep `id-token: write` on the publish job only, and keep the Release environment protected.

pins: src/Transloadit/Transloadit.csproj: Version 0.11.0, TargetFrameworks (12), LangVersion 12, Microsoft.SourceLink.GitHub 8.0.0, System.Text.Json 8.0.5, Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.1, CheckEolTargetFramework=false, DebugType=embedded, SignAssembly=True (no key file)

Planned deviation fixes (each its own change): enable package validation with a baseline; switch symbols to .snupkg; adopt a real strong-name key before 1.0 (identity change, release declared breaking); set AssemblyVersion to major-only and adjust ProjectTests; drop out-of-support TFMs and CheckEolTargetFramework=false in a release declared breaking; obsolete-then-remove for all future public API removals
lockStep: AssemblyVersion major (once set) <-> package major version
Strong-name key <-> InternalsVisibleTo public key <-> test project signing
deploy.yml file name + Release environment <-> nuget.org Trusted Publishing policy
Removed TFMs <-> CompatibilitySuppressions.xml entries <-> release notes

Microsoft.SourceLink.GitHub and Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies release notes and latest versions: not read. The pack recommends relying on the SDK's built-in Source Link rather than a specific newer pin.
Official confirmation that Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies is referenced implicitly by current SDKs: a search found only secondary hints, so no rule was written about removing it.

System.Text.Json 8.0.x servicing after .NET 8 end of support (2026-11-10): no page read on the package's post-EOL servicing or the recommended next floor (9.x/10.x) for netstandard2.0/net462 consumers.
questions: Strong naming (known deviation, rule 7): SignAssembly=True has no key file, and InternalsVisibleTo names an unsigned friend, so the shipped DLL is most likely unsigned while CLAUDE.md says it is signed. Please confirm on a built DLL (sn -v or its public key token). Then adopt a committed key (or public key + PublicSign) in a release declared breaking, ideally before 1.0, and correct CLAUDE.md.

Per-TFM public API: SystemTextJsonSerializer is public on netstandard2.0/net462+, while NewtonsoftJsonSerializer, TransloaditSerializerSettings, AnyOfConverter, BooleanToIntConverter and the DateTime converters are public only on net452/net461. Package validation will flag the netstandard2.0 vs net461 gap. Options: (a) drop net452/net461 (out of support since 2022-04-26) so every asset shares the STJ surface, (b) make the engine-specific types internal and keep only ITransloaditSerializer/TransloaditSerializerFactory public, or (c) accept and suppress with a documented CompatibilitySuppressions.xml.

Was the previously published version's public surface Newtonsoft-based on all TFMs (as CLAUDE.md's 'only runtime dependency is Newtonsoft.Json' suggests)? If so, the move to System.Text.Json removed public types such as TransloaditSerializerSettings and AnyOfConverter from most TFMs without an [Obsolete] release. That is a breaking change the next release notes should call out, and the baseline validator will report it.

Breaking changes in 0.x (known deviation, rule 2): from now on, every removal goes through obsolete-then-remove plus package validation. Should the library also go to 1.0.0 (SemVer FAQ: used in production, users depend on the API) so that later breaks require a major bump?

AssemblyVersion (known deviation, rule 8): moving to major-only AssemblyVersion while the package is 0.x would pin it at 0.0.0.0 for every 0.x release. Should that wait until 1.0, or should 0.x minor bumps be treated as majors for AssemblyVersion (0.Y.0.0) until then? Either way, ProjectTests must stop asserting AssemblyVersion == ClientVersion.Current.
Symbols (known deviation, rule 6): switch from embedded PDBs to a .snupkg pushed next to the .nupkg in deploy.yml?
EOL targets (known deviation, rule 13): which release drops net452, net461, net5.0, net6.0 and net7.0 (and net8.0/net9.0 after 2026-11-10), and with what notice to .NET Framework 4.5.2/4.6.1 users?

CLAUDE.md describes Newtonsoft.Json as the only runtime dependency and TransloaditSerializerSettings as the default config. The csproj now uses System.Text.Json on every TFM except net452/net461. Should CLAUDE.md be updated?
